entities.name: Precordial paste bridge effects
observations: No direct PubMed experiment specifically tested a continuous conductive paste bridge between standard V1–V6 electrodes; available evidence is mechanistic or analogous.
A wet conductive bridge can lower inter-electrode impedance, partially equalize neighboring electrode potentials, and cause cross-talk or signal mixing.
Expected effects include disrupted R-wave progression, altered QRS and ST-T amplitudes or polarity, baseline shifts, and possible saturation with very low impedance.
Contact/impedance artifacts can selectively distort precordial ST-T segments and QT and mimic ischemia; repeat recording is required before diagnosis.

entities.name: PMID:40152640
observations: A precordial contact-related artifact produced pseudo-ST depression and apparent QT prolongation, illustrating that contact/impedance artifacts can mimic ischemia.

entities.name: PMID:34595053
observations: The report identifies loose or dried electrodes, substances on skin, faulty wires, and poor contact as causes of baseline artifact and pseudo-ST elevation.

entities.name: PMID:30965742
observations: Conductive carbon paste can provide a low-impedance skin interface for ECG recording, supporting the plausibility that a spread paste film can electrically couple nearby electrode sites.
